newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Coffee-Colombian strike seen adding to supply woes.
newsitem.headline: Coffee-Colombian strike seen adding to supply woes.

text.p: With a strike by Colombian truck drivers set to begin at midnight Saturday, the world's second leading coffee producer looks certain to deepen the near-term supply concerns that drove prices to a 2-1/2 year high this week.

Spokesmen for the Colombian Truck Drivers' Association (ACC), which represents about 80 percent of Colombia's truckers, said late Wednesday that the nationwide strike was almost certain to go forward since negotiations with the government broke off over a week earlier and there had been no attempt by government officials to renew them.
That strike paralyzed virtually all of the country's highway freight including about 200,000 60-kg bags of coffee.

Coffee exporters, with memories of the October stoppage still fresh in their minds, have rushed about 420,000 70-kg bags to port in the last week in a bid to ensure that April export deadlines would not be missed.
But industry sources say the new strike could wreak havoc with May export schedules if it lasts more than about 10 days.
Jorge Cardenas, head of the National Coffee Growers' Federation, spoke of the strike threat and its potential impact on the coffee market earlier this week.
"It could do serious damage to coffee flows over the next few weeks," he told reporters. "The market is going to be nervous and it's going to be concerned," he said.
"Any interruption in Colombia (coffee supplies) would have a very negative effect," Cardenas added.
Further adding to market supply woes, Cardenas said Colombia produced just 10 million 60-kg bags of coffee in April 1996 through March 1997, down from about 14 million bags in same period 1995/96.
He did not elaborate on causes of the 4 million bag drop in output, but heavy rains at the start of the year were widely seen as a factor that would cut into overall production.

Underscoring the tight supply situation, federation sources said Wednesday that Colombia's coffee exports fell 20 percent in March compared to the same month last year, from 910,861 to 727,960 60-kg bags.
Ironically, industry sources say some exporters were left holding the bag Monday when the federation announced that it was closing registrations for May/June coffee shipments with immediate effect.

The sources, who asked not be be identified by name, said the abrupt announcement left several exporters who failed to register May/June shipments in time holding onto considerable amounts of fresh green coffee.
Cardenas said registrations were closed because private exporters had already filled their 1,250,000-bag export quota for April/June.

It was not immediately clear when registrations would be opened for shipments in July, but federation sources said it was unlikely to happen any time before next month's Association of Coffeee Producing Countries' meeting in London.
